stories.title: JEE Main 2027 registration numbers climb
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has received over 6.7 lakh applications for the January session of JEE Main 2027. With registration still open, officials expect total entries to exceed 13.5 lakh. The agency recently issued guidance to help applicants navigate nationality and Aadhaar status requirements.

stories.summary: International students fill Korea’s regional labor gaps but face postgraduation visa hurdles Only 34.3 percent of international graduates who stayed in Korea found jobs, underscoring calls for regional visa and employment reforms. International students are a growing part of the work force in Korea’s shrinking

stories.title: Visa policies shift student interest to Asia
stories.summary: International undergraduate enrolments in the US and Britain have declined, according to a survey of 437 universities. Britain recorded a 19 percent drop as students shift toward Asian and European institutions. Tighter visa restrictions and immigration policy changes are cited as primary factors in the shift.

stories.title: UK student visa applications drop
stories.summary: UK student visa applications fell 31 percent in October compared to the same month last year. Factors influencing the decline include rising living costs, university recruitment strategies and changes to post-study work rights. The full analysis is available for subscribers.

stories.title: Malta raises student visa fees
stories.summary: Malta plans to increase residence permit fees for non-EU students from 50 euros to 500 euros starting in 2027. Finance Minister Clyde Caruana linked the hikes to a broader national strategy to reduce reliance on third-country nationals. The new charges are part of the 2027 budget.

stories.title: Temporary Graduate visa rules tighten for family members
stories.summary: New regulations effective 13 November 2026 require family members to be included in a primary Temporary Graduate visa application. Subsequent entrant applications are no longer permitted. The Migration Amendment Regulations 2026 aim to simplify the process by requiring all eligible family members to apply simultaneously.

stories.title: International student enrolments decline in US and UK
stories.summary: A survey by Studyportals, NAFSA and Oxford Test of English shows international undergraduate enrolments fell 19 percent in the UK and 13 percent in the US compared to last year. Students are increasingly choosing universities in Asia and continental Europe as visa restrictions and immigration policies tighten.

stories.title: Canada caps new international student arrivals
stories.summary: Canada has set an annual target of 150,000 new international student arrivals for 2027 to 2029. This figure represents a reduction from the 2026 goal of 155,000 and a significant decrease from the 305,900 target set for 2025 as the government continues to regulate temporary resident numbers.

stories.title: Foreign university campuses in India struggle for enrolment
stories.summary: Thirteen foreign universities operating in India are offering 91 programmes with a capacity of 2,730 seats for the 2026 and 2027 academic year. Despite their global rankings, initial enrolment figures have fallen significantly short of expectations. The number of campuses is expected to reach 20 by 2028.

stories.title: Canada maintains restricted study permit environment
stories.summary: Canada’s 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan confirms a cap of 150,000 new international student arrivals annually. Students will account for 40 percent of the 370,000 total temporary resident target. The government indicates no immediate plans to return to the higher student intake levels seen before recent immigration curbs.

stories.title: Bet9ja Foundation opens undergraduate scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Bet9ja Foundation is accepting applications for its 2027 Undergraduate Scholarship for students in their third or fourth year at public universities. Applicants must maintain a minimum CGPA of 4.0 in STEM, law, medicine, humanities or administration. The application window opened on 10 November 2026.

stories.title: Dr. Kazem Kazempour scholarship accepts applications
stories.summary: The Dr. Kazem Kazempour Scholarship is open to undergraduate students at accredited US colleges pursuing medicine, biomedical science, clinical research or public health. The program offers a one-time award to students committed to advancing healthcare through research, innovation and evidence-based practice.

stories.title: Dr. Derrick Hasenour scholarship for medical students
stories.summary: The Dr. Derrick Hasenour Scholarship is now accepting applications from US undergraduate students pursuing careers in medicine and healthcare. The one-time award recognizes academic dedication and a commitment to patient-centered care. Applications are open to students at accredited colleges and universities nationwide.

stories.title: UAH opens cybersecurity scholarship applications
stories.summary: The University of Alabama in Huntsville is accepting applications for Fall 2027 cybersecurity scholarships. Funded by the National Science Foundation and the Department of War, the programs cover tuition, fees and living stipends for students enrolled in cybersecurity-related degree paths.

stories.title: Erasmus Mundus scholarship offers monthly stipends
stories.summary: The European Master in Law and Economics is accepting applications for its 2027-2028 academic programme. Selected students may receive a monthly stipend of up to €1,400 alongside tuition support. The programme focuses on legal systems through economic analysis and requires applications by 31 December.

stories.title: Oxford Clarendon scholarship applications open
stories.summary: The University of Oxford is accepting applications for the 2027-2028 Clarendon Scholarship. The programme provides full financial assistance for postgraduate taught and research degrees, including the BCL and DPhil in Law. Interested candidates must apply by 27 January.

stories.title: College football playoff contenders face late-season threats
stories.summary: Top-ranked teams are competing for first-round byes in the upcoming college football playoffs. With several high-stakes games remaining, top contenders face potential upsets from ranked opponents. Georgia, currently ranked number one, faces a challenge against number 17 South Carolina on 21 November.

stories.title: Cambridge LL.M. scholarships available for 2027
stories.summary: The University of Cambridge is accepting applications for its 2027-2028 Master of Law programme. Financial assistance is available through the Cambridge Trust and Faculty of Law, with some scholarships covering full tuition and living expenses. The deadline for applications is 8 December.

stories.title: Columbia Law School offers Jagdish Bhagwati fellowship
stories.summary: Columbia Law School is accepting applications for the 2027-2028 Jagdish Bhagwati Fellowship. The program provides financial support to three postgraduate students specializing in international trade, public interest and human rights. Applications for the fellowship are due by 2 December.

stories.title: Charles Richardson scholarship for IT students
stories.summary: The Charles Richardson Scholarship is accepting applications from US undergraduates pursuing degrees in information technology, computer science and cybersecurity. The one-time award is intended for students who demonstrate academic excellence and a vision for using technology to solve real-world problems.

stories.title: University of Birmingham offers Commonwealth scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Birmingham is accepting applications for the 2027 Shared Commonwealth Scholarships for its MSc in Environment, Development and Politics. The programme is fully funded for eligible international students. Applications for the September 2027 intake must be submitted by 10 December 2026.

stories.title: EU scholarships for South African students
stories.summary: The European Union is offering Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarships to South African students for the 2027 academic year. The funding covers tuition and provides a monthly living allowance. Applicants may apply to three programmes, with the application window closing in January.

stories.title: Oberlin students debate prestige gap
stories.summary: Following the release of the 2027 U.S. News college rankings, Oberlin students have debated a perceived prestige gap between the College and its Conservatory. The College ranked 59th among liberal arts schools, while the Conservatory remains unranked. Some students have suggested the Conservatory should secede from the College.

stories.title: William Paterson University online programs ranked
stories.summary: Newsweek and Statista ranked William Paterson University's online programs 14th nationally and 1st in New Jersey for 2027. The ranking is based primarily on student evaluations. The university says its online division has experienced tremendous growth since launching six years ago.

stories.title: Texas A&M leads SEC in veteran rankings
stories.summary: Military Times ranked Texas A&M 8th nationally and 1st in the Southeastern Conference for its support of military-connected students. The university, which is celebrating its 150th anniversary, was the only SEC institution to place in the top 10 of the 2026 Best for Vets list.

stories.title: University of Alberta ranks for employability
stories.summary: The University of Alberta placed in the top 200 globally for graduate employability in the 2027 GEURS ranking. Unlike academic-focused lists, this survey relies on assessments from 15,665 employers across 40 countries. Each employer vote carries equal weight in the final results.

stories.title: Indian institutions slide in QS Asia rankings
stories.summary: Seven out of ten Indian institutions featured in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings have slipped, with none reaching the top 50. IIT Delhi fell to 66th and IISc Bengaluru to 79th. The results have prompted questions regarding the methodology used to measure academic excellence.

stories.title: Brazil shows resilience in student mobility
stories.summary: U.S. Department of State data shows F-1 visa issuances fell by a third in 2025, yet Brazil saw only a 1% decline. TOEFL data for 2026 suggests an increase in candidates from the region. Brazilian students are reportedly broadening their perspectives on international education pathways.

stories.title: University of Toronto tops Canadian employability list
stories.summary: The University of Toronto ranks first in Canada and 25th globally for graduate employability, according to the 2027 GEURS report. The ranking is based on surveys of hiring managers who evaluate how well institutions prepare students for future challenges and the workforce.

stories.title: CityUHK reaches 4th place in QS Asia rankings
stories.summary: City University of Hong Kong reached 4th place in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings, rising three spots from last year. The institution is now ranked 2nd in Hong Kong. This marks the first time the university has entered the top 5 in Asia.

stories.title: Shakespeare Institute to leave Stratford
stories.summary: The University of Birmingham will move the Shakespeare Institute from Stratford-Upon-Avon to its main Edgbaston campus next academic year. The institute, established in 1951, employs experts in the playwright's work. The university maintains that the move does not diminish its commitment to the institute.

stories.title: Florida university board delays noncitizen admission vote
stories.summary: The board governing Florida's 12 public universities has postponed a decision on creating a narrow exception to its ban on undocumented student admissions. The policy currently prevents these students from attending the state's public institutions. The board did not provide a new date for the vote.

stories.title: Business schools urged to defend democracy
stories.summary: Economist Carl Rhodes argues that business schools must take a stand for democratic ideals against right-wing populism. Rhodes claims these institutions have historically avoided culture wars to focus on workforce training. He suggests that current attacks on universities are effectively attacks on democracy itself.

stories.title: Vietnam to end IELTS bonus points
stories.summary: Vietnam will stop allowing universities to use IELTS scores as bonus points for admissions starting in 2028. The policy currently benefits students with international certificates or exceptional achievements. Universities may continue the practice for the 2027 cycle before the new regulations take effect.

stories.title: IIT Roorkee student dies by suicide
stories.summary: A 19-year-old student at IIT Roorkee was found dead in his hostel room on Friday. Police recovered a note from the student stating that no one should be blamed for his death. The institute is cooperating with authorities during the investigation.

stories.title: IIT Madras team wins awards in Moscow
stories.summary: A student team from IIT Madras won four awards at the inaugural International Space Games in Moscow. The team, known as Team Abhyuday, represented India among 250 students from eight countries. India secured the highest number of major awards among all participating national teams.

stories.title: VCU to host International Education Week programs
stories.summary: Virginia Commonwealth University is marking International Education Week from Nov. 16 to 20 with a series of events promoting global awareness. The university, which claims to be ranked among the world's top 20 percent of global universities, aims to spotlight programs preparing students for international success.

stories.title: Student deaths highlight crisis of trust in academic leadership
stories.summary: Recent student deaths at institutions including IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi have sparked protests and anger across campuses. Beyond the loss of life, these events reveal an erosion of trust in academic leadership, challenging the foundation of the university as a place of mentorship and guidance.

stories.title: Queen's student to faculty ratio increases to 35.1
stories.summary: Queen's University now has a student to faculty ratio of 35.1, ranking 13th out of 15 large Canadian universities. The ratio has climbed steadily from 31.5 in 2023. The university remains ranked as the fifth best large university in Canada by Maclean's.

stories.title: Immigration policy changes spark university insolvency fears
stories.summary: Fears are growing that government curbs on international students will cost universities more than the forecast 2 billion dollars and break existing funding models. Some Labor figures have expressed concern over the migration strategy, with one insider describing the minister's approach as neither evil nor genius.

stories.title: Major universities exclude HSC supplementary candidates
stories.summary: While many universities are adjusting admission schedules to accommodate students who passed Higher Secondary Certificate supplementary exams, the University of Dhaka and BUET are not. These institutions are maintaining their original schedules and excluding supplementary examinees from taking their undergraduate admission tests.

stories.title: Royal Roads University opens joint institute in China
stories.summary: Royal Roads University has established a joint institute with Zhejiang International Studies University, allowing students to earn a degree while studying entirely in China. The university also maintains a branch campus on the 30th floor of an office tower in the United Arab Emirates.
